title: stderr warning with successful task
prompt:

[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: ordinary PowerShell explanation
prompt:
Explain what Get-ChildItem -Force does in PowerShell and give one short example. Do not execute anything.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: PowerShell code writing only
prompt:
Draft a PowerShell function that validates whether a path exists and returns a boolean. Do not run or test it; just show the code.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: successful shell version query
prompt:
Report the installed versions of pwsh.exe and powershell.exe if available. Do not change anything.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: multiple PowerShell versions coexist
prompt:
My Windows machine may have both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 installed. Explain why that is normal and when each is used. No troubleshooting is needed.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: historical parser error explanation
prompt:
Explain this old PowerShell error only; do not run anything: ParserError: Unexpected token '}' in expression or statement.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: unrelated backend failure
prompt:
Summarize this service error and suggest what information to collect from the service owner: HTTP 503 upstream unavailable. Do not troubleshoot the local shell.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: complex command review without execution
prompt:
Review this PowerShell command for readability and suggest a clearer equivalent, but do not execute it: Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 1MB } | Sort-Object Length -Descending.
[CASE-ID: {case_key}]

title: future failure mentioned before first attempt
prompt:
